sentences.zh: 所以，这当然是阿尔弗雷德·丁尼生勋爵的作品。

sentences.en: I mean, you describe this,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，汤姆，

sentences.en: Tom, as the most famous poem ever written about a cavalry charge.
sentences.zh: 你将这首诗形容为有史以来最著名的关于骑兵冲锋的诗作。

sentences.en: It's one of the great poems, let's be honeSt. He's describing, of course, the suicidal charge of the Light Brigade on the 26th of September, 1854.
sentences.zh: 说实话，它是最伟大的诗篇之一。他描绘的当然是1854年9月26日轻骑兵旅那次自杀式的冲锋。

sentences.en: They're charging a Russian battery of these massive guns.
sentences.zh: 他们正在向俄国人的一个装备重型火炮的炮兵阵地冲锋。

sentences.en: So this is one of the most heroic failures in British military history, as he describes in the poem.
sentences.zh: 正如他在诗中所描绘的那样，这是英国军事史上最英勇却也最惨烈的失败之一。

sentences.en: They're sabring the gunners.
sentences.zh: 他们正在劈砍炮手。

sentences.en: They're charging an army.
sentences.zh: 他们正在向军队冲锋。

sentences.en: They're breaking through the line.
sentences.zh: 他们正在冲破防线。

sentences.en: Cossacks and Russians are reeling under the impact of the Light Brigade's attack.
sentences.zh: 哥萨克人和俄国人在轻骑兵旅的猛烈攻击下节节败退。

sentences.en: And it comes at this hideous cost, which is, of course, why it's immortalized in British literature.
sentences.zh: 但这付出了极其惨重的代价，当然，这也是它得以在英国文学中永垂不朽的原因。

sentences.en: And yes, at the same time, as you point out, this is precisely what the Light Brigade have been dreaming of all these long months and indeed years of relative inaction.
sentences.zh: 是的，正如你所指出的，与此同时，这正是轻骑兵旅在经历了漫长数月甚至数年的相对无所作为后，梦寐以求的时刻。

sentences.en: This is their moment.
sentences.zh: 这就是他们的时刻。

sentences.en: This is their chance to prove their British courage.
sentences.zh: 这是他们证明英国人勇气的机会。

sentences.en: And of course, Lord Cardigan, the man in charge, what a great character he is.
sentences.zh: 当然，负责指挥的卡迪根勋爵，他可真是个个性鲜明的人物。

sentences.en: He has never seen active service, has he, up to this point?
sentences.zh: 在此之前，他从未经历过实战，对吧？

sentences.en: And nor have most of his men.
sentences.zh: 他手下的绝大多数人也是如此。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And I think that for Cardigan, for his men, for years, this had been a source of frustration.
sentences.zh: 我认为对卡迪根以及他的部下而言，多年来这一直是一种挫败感的来源。

sentences.en: They were all itching to put their relentless training into practice, to give their foes a taste of cold British steel, all of that.
sentences.zh: 他们都迫不及待地想把不间断的训练付诸实践，让敌人尝尝英国精钢的厉害，诸如此类。

sentences.en: But they haven't been able to because Britain hasn't been engaged in a land war on Europe.
sentences.zh: 但他们一直无法做到，因为英国没有参与欧洲的大陆战争。

sentences.en: And then suddenly, as we heard in our last episode, in spring 1854, that changes.
sentences.zh: 然而突然之间，正如我们在上一集听到的那样，在1854年春，情况变了。

sentences.en: And the British and French, old enemies, of course, but now in alliance, declare war on Russia.
sentences.zh: 英国和法国——这对老敌人，当然，现在结成了同盟——向俄国宣战了。

sentences.en: And their goal is to stop a Russian advance on Constantinople, the key strategic city, which controls access between the Mediterranean Sea and the Black Sea.
sentences.zh: 他们的目标是阻止俄国军队向君士坦丁堡推进。君士坦丁堡是一个关键的战略城市，控制着地中海与黑海之间的交通要道。

sentences.en: And so the British go out there, and among them, Lord Cardigan and his Light Brigade, and they're eager to get stuck in.
sentences.zh: 于是英国军队开赴前线，其中包括卡迪根勋爵和他的轻骑兵旅，他们都渴望大干一场。

sentences.en: But it's either a glorious triumph or a massive problem, depending on your perspective.
sentences.zh: 但从不同的角度来看，这要么是一场辉煌的胜利，要么是一个巨大的麻烦。

sentences.en: But the Turks, whom the British and French had expected would roll over in the face of the Russian advance, instead put up this heroic defence.
sentences.zh: 然而，英国和法国原本以为在俄军进攻面前会一触即溃的土耳其人，却展开了英勇的抵抗。

sentences.en: Because the Turk, they believed, had been enfeebled by abominations.
sentences.zh: 因为他们曾认为土耳其人已经因种种陋习而衰弱不堪。

sentences.en: But no, that was a complete misreading.
sentences.zh: 但事实并非如此，那完全是误读。

sentences.en: Not for the last time.
sentences.zh: 而且这并非最后一次。

sentences.en: Well, they might have been engaging in abominations, but it hasn't enfeebled them, would be the alternative perspective on that.
sentences.zh: 好吧，从另一个角度来看，他们或许确实沉迷于某些陋习，但这并没有使他们虚弱。

sentences.en: But it's inspired and roused them.
sentences.zh: 反而激发并振奋了他们。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Whatever.
sentences.zh: 随它去吧。

sentences.en: The Turk has stood strong and tall and has seen the Russians off.
sentences.zh: 土耳其人坚定不移地挺立着，击退了俄国人。

sentences.en: And by late June, the Turks have succeeded in forcing a Russian retreat.
sentences.zh: 到6月下旬，土耳其人成功迫使俄军撤退。

sentences.en: And the French and the British, you know, they've arrived too late to see any action.
sentences.zh: 而法军和英军呢，他们赶到时已经错过了所有的战斗。

sentences.en: So they've gone all this way.
sentences.zh: 所以他们大老远跑了这一趟。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And there's no chance to have a go at the Russians and win glory for themselves.
sentences.zh: 结果连跟俄国人交手、为自己赢得荣誉的机会都没有。

sentences.en: But Lord Cardigan has been riding around.
sentences.zh: 但卡迪根勋爵一直在四处骑马巡视。

sentences.en: Has he in a performative manner?
sentences.zh: 他是不是在摆出一副作秀的姿态？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So he has been sent by Lord Raglan, the British commander in chief, to go and reconnoiter the Danube, which the Russians have been trying to cross,
sentences.zh: 他被英国远征军总司令拉格朗勋爵派去侦察多瑙河——俄国人一直在试图渡过多瑙河——

sentences.en: and to see whether the Russian withdrawal is actually true and whether it's everything that the Turks have been saying.
sentences.zh: 并查看俄军撤退是否属实，是否真如土耳其人所说的那样。

sentences.en: And so he goes up to the Danube from the Light Brigade's base in
sentences.zh: 于是他从轻骑兵旅位于

sentences.en: Bulgaria.
sentences.zh: 保加利亚的基地出发，前往多瑙河。

sentences.en: And he observes the Russians on the far bank.
sentences.zh: 他在对岸观察俄军。

sentences.en: And he, you know, he's able to confirm that the Russians have indeed withdrawn from the south bank of the Danube.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道的，他得以证实俄军确实已经从多瑙河南岸撤离了。

sentences.en: But neither the British nor the Russians try to engage with one another.
sentences.zh: 但无论是英国人还是俄国人都没有试图与对方交战。

sentences.en: And the most that the two sides do is to inspect each other through telescopes.
sentences.zh: 双方最多不过是通过望远镜互相观察一番。

sentences.en: And so I think not just the Light Brigade, but the entire Allied expedition feels an intense sense of frustration because the Turks have won glory for themselves.
sentences.zh: 所以我想，不仅是轻骑兵旅，整个盟军远征军都感到了一种强烈的挫败感，因为土耳其人赢得了属于他们自己的荣耀。

sentences.en: But when are the French and the British going to have a chance to win glory?
sentences.zh: 但法军和英军什么时候才能有机会赢得荣耀呢？

sentences.en: And unusually in this campaign, we described before how it's often seen as the first modern war, they are under public pressure, partly because of newspaper reporting, aren't they?
sentences.zh: 不同寻常的是，在这次战役中——我们之前描述过它常被视为第一场现代战争——他们承受着来自公众的压力，部分原因是因为报纸的报道，不是吗？

sentences.en: I mean, this is a key element of the Crimean War.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这是克里米亚战争的一个关键要素。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And so our key witness to all this is a man called William Howard Russell.
sentences.zh: 因此，我们了解这一切的关键见证人是一个名叫威廉·霍华德·拉塞尔的人。

sentences.en: We mentioned him in our last episode.
sentences.zh: 我们在上一集提到过他。

sentences.en: And he is an Irish journalist who's been sent by the Times to cover the entire duration of the war.
sentences.zh: 他是一位爱尔兰记者，被《泰晤士报》派去报道整场战争的全过程。

sentences.en: And this is a first for a British military campaign.
sentences.zh: 这在英国军事战役中尚属首次。

sentences.en: And so he's in Bulgaria, and he's reporting the mood of the British camp back to his readers in Britain.
sentences.zh: 所以他在保加利亚，向英国本土的读者报道英国军营的精神面貌。

sentences.en: And he writes, the prominent feeling among the men was one of disappointment, lest they should lose the chance after coming so far of having one last brush with the Russians.
sentences.zh: 他写道：“士兵们心头最强烈的情绪是一种失望，唯恐在大老远赶来之后，会失去与俄国人进行最后一次交锋的机会。”

sentences.en: But in the event, the men do get their chance.
sentences.zh: 但事实上，士兵们确实得到了他们的机会。

sentences.en: Because on the 7th of September, the British and French set sail from Varna, which was a picturesque, charming little seaside resort.
sentences.zh: 因为在9月7日，英法联军从瓦尔纳起航，那曾是一个风景优美、迷人的海滨度假胜地。

sentences.en: And over the previous three months has become a cholera-ridden
sentences.zh: 但在过去三个月里，它已经变成了一个霍乱肆虐的

sentences.en: cesspit.
sentences.zh: 粪坑。

sentences.en: It's on the coast of Bulgaria.
sentences.zh: 它位于保加利亚海岸。

sentences.en: And everybody who's been staying there, the kind of the great mass of the British and French, tens of thousands of men, are incredibly glad to be shot of the place,
sentences.zh: 所有曾滞留在那里的英法大部队——数万名官兵——都对终于能离开这个鬼地方感到无比高兴，

sentences.en: because they've all been dying of various ailments and diseases.
sentences.zh: 因为他们当中有太多人死于各种小毛病和疾病。

sentences.en: And they head out to sea.
sentences.zh: 于是他们扬帆出海。

sentences.en: Although they don't all go, do they?
sentences.zh: 尽管他们并没有全部离开，对吧？

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 没有。

sentences.en: They leave some of them behind.
sentences.zh: 他们留下了一些人。

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So there are about 90,000 in all, and only about 60,000 go.
sentences.zh: 总人数大约有9万，但只有大约6万人出发了。

sentences.en: And the reason for this is because there aren't enough transport ships to take them all in one go.
sentences.zh: 原因是没有足够的运输船把他们一次性全部运走。

sentences.en: And among those left behind are the heavy brigade.
sentences.zh: 留下来的人当中就包括重骑兵旅。

sentences.en: So the British cavalry have two brigades, the light brigade and the heavy brigade.
sentences.zh: 英国骑兵有两个旅，轻骑兵旅和重骑兵旅。

sentences.en: The heavy brigade stay behind.
sentences.zh: 重骑兵旅留在了后方。

sentences.en: And the reason for that is that there aren't enough transport ships.
sentences.zh: 原因就是缺乏运输船。

sentences.en: And so once the light brigade has been delivered, they'll go back and they'll pick up the horses and the heavy brigade and bring the heavy brigade across.
sentences.zh: 所以一旦轻骑兵旅被运送到目的地，船只就会返回，接上马匹和重骑兵旅，然后再将重骑兵旅运过海峡。

sentences.en: So just for people to bear in mind, in the opening weeks of the looming campaign, there's no heavy brigade, only the light brigade.
sentences.zh: 因此，大家需要记住的是，在即将到来的战役的最初几周里，并没有重骑兵旅，只有轻骑兵旅。

sentences.en: And also going with the French and the British are some 7,000 Turks who are veterans of their recent heroics on the Danube.
sentences.zh: 随法军和英军一同前往的还有大约7000名土耳其人，他们是最近在多瑙河英勇作战的老兵。

sentences.en: But do these people know where they are going?
sentences.zh: 但这些人知道他们要去哪里吗？

sentences.en: I mean, they don't, do they?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他们不知道，对吧？

sentences.en: A lot of the
sentences.zh: 许多

sentences.en: British soldiers thought they were there to fight the French anyway.
sentences.zh: 英国士兵甚至以为他们去那里是为了跟法国人打仗。

sentences.en: Or the Turk.
sentences.zh: 或者跟土耳其人打仗。

sentences.en: This must be very confusing for them to get on these transport ships and then head off across the Black Sea to God knows where.
sentences.zh: 登上这些运输船，然后驶过黑海去天知道什么地方，这一定让他们感到非常困惑。

sentences.en: And actually, do the commanders know where they're going and what the plan is?
sentences.zh: 说真的，指挥官们知道自己要去哪里以及计划是什么吗？

sentences.en: I mean, the scale of confusion and muddle in this campaign is off the scale.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这场战役中的混乱和糊涂程度简直无以复加。

sentences.en: And as you say, the men don't really know where they're going or why.
sentences.zh: 正如你所说，士兵们并不真正知道他们要去哪里，也不知道为什么要去。

sentences.en: And the same is true of the commanders, because confusion reaches all the way to the top.
sentences.zh: 指挥官们也是如此，因为混乱一直蔓延到了最高层。

sentences.en: And there's a perfect symbol of this.
sentences.zh: 有一个完美的象征可以说明这一点。

sentences.en: So there is Lord Raglan, the British commander, and then there is his French opposite number,
sentences.zh: 那就是英国指挥官拉格朗勋爵，以及他的法军对等官员，

sentences.en: Le Roy de Saint-Arnaud.
sentences.zh: 勒鲁瓦·德·圣阿尔诺。

sentences.en: And they're sailing in different ships, but they can't meet each other face to face as they're sailing across the Black Sea to their ultimate destination, which is the
sentences.zh: 他们乘坐不同的船只航行，但在穿越黑海前往最终目的地——

sentences.en: Crimea.
sentences.zh: 克里米亚——的航程中，他们无法面对面会面。

sentences.en: And the reason for that is that Raglan, he had fought at Waterloo and lost an arm there.
sentences.zh: 原因在于，拉格朗曾在滑铁卢战役中作战并在那里失去了一条手臂。

sentences.en: And so he finds it very difficult to clamber up the side of a ship because he's only got one arm.
sentences.zh: 因此，由于只有一只胳膊，他发现攀爬船舷非常困难。

sentences.en: And then you have Saint-Arnaud, a former fencing instructor.
sentences.zh: 而圣阿尔诺呢，曾是一名击剑教练。

sentences.en: Yeah, the dancing master.
sentences.zh: 对，那个舞蹈大师。

sentences.zh: 有点像个骗子。不过必须承认，他也是个相当残忍且高效的军事指挥官。

sentences.en: But he, unfortunately, has been suffering from terrible intestinal complaints.
sentences.zh: 但遗憾的是，他一直遭受着可怕的肠胃疾病折磨。

sentences.en: Oh yeah, you mentioned this.
sentences.zh: 哦对，你提过这个。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.zh: 最近被诊断为晚期胃癌。

sentences.en: Oh my God.
sentences.zh: 噢天哪。

sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And so it's suboptimal, I think, in terms of inter-army discussion.
sentences.zh: 因此，我认为这对于军队之间的沟通来说并不是最理想的状态。

sentences.en: Definitely.
sentences.zh: 绝对如此。

sentences.en: And so Raglan and Saint-Arnaud have to communicate entirely through intermediaries.
sentences.zh: 所以拉格朗和圣阿尔诺只能完全通过中间人来沟通。

sentences.en: And then, of course, there's opportunities for Chinese whispers, for confusion, misunderstandings, whatever.
sentences.zh: 当然，这就带来了以讹传讹、混淆视听、产生误解的种种机会。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: There are going to be some interesting misunderstandings in the next two episodes, aren't there?
sentences.zh: 在接下来的两集里，会有一些有趣的误解，不是吗？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Now, underlying all this is surely a deeper issue, which is the British and the French went to war in order to prevent the Russians from seizing Constantinople and dismembering
sentences.zh: 而这一切的背后，无疑存在着一个更深层次的问题，那就是英法参战是为了阻止俄国人夺取君士坦丁堡并瓜分

sentences.en: the Ottoman Empire.
sentences.zh: 奥斯曼帝国。

sentences.en: The Russians have now been seen off.
sentences.zh: 俄国人现在已经被赶走了。

sentences.en: They've been, they've retreated from the Balkans.
sentences.zh: 他们已经、他们已经从巴尔干半岛撤退了。

sentences.en: So Constantinople is safe.
sentences.zh: 所以君士坦丁堡是安全的。

sentences.en: So as we said last time, the British and French could at this point say, well, we have actually now won this war and we will go home.
sentences.zh: 正如我们上次所说，英国人和法国人在这个时候可以说，好吧，我们实际上已经赢得了这场战争，我们要回家了。

sentences.en: What they're doing is they're heading out across the Black Sea, as you already said, towards the Crimean Peninsula.
sentences.zh: 正如你刚才所说，他们现在正穿过黑海，朝克里米亚半岛进发。

sentences.en: The obvious question is, is why?
sentences.zh: 显而易见的问题是，为什么？

sentences.en: I mean, it's not like they're going to capture the Russian Empire.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他们又不是要去占领俄罗斯帝国。

sentences.en: Why bother going?
sentences.zh: 为什么非要去呢？

sentences.en: You know, what's the military rationale for this campaign?
sentences.zh: 你知道，这次行动的军事逻辑是什么？

sentences.en: So their target is Sebastopol, a great port and the base of Russia's Black Sea fleet.
sentences.zh: 所以他们的目标是塞瓦斯托波尔，一个伟大的港口，也是俄国黑海舰队的基地。

sentences.en: And the reason why it might make military sense to capture Sebastopol is that if they can eliminate Russia's Black Sea fleet, then obviously that means that Constantinople will
sentences.zh: 占领塞瓦斯托波尔在军事上可能说得通的原因在于，如果他们能消灭俄国的黑海舰队，那么显然这意味着君士坦丁堡将

sentences.en: be secure, not just for a year or two, but for potentially for decades.
sentences.zh: 得到保障，不仅是一两年，而且可能是几十年。

sentences.en: So Tom, I can't believe you haven't made this point already.
sentences.zh: 所以，汤姆，我真不敢相信你刚才还没提到这一点。

sentences.en: I'm about to beat you to it.
sentences.zh: 我正要抢先说出来呢。

sentences.en: I mean, this is a point that really belongs to you, certainly emotionally.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这其实是一个真正属于你的观点，至少在情感上是这样。

sentences.en: They're attacking the Chatham of Russia, of the Russian Empire.
sentences.zh: 他们正在攻击俄罗斯帝国的查塔姆。

sentences.en: This is like the French or the Dutch attack in Chatham.
sentences.zh: 这就像法国人或荷兰人进攻查塔姆一样。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So it was Napoleon's aim to capture the naval dockyards at Portsmouth and Chatham and burn them.
sentences.zh: 因此，拿破仑的目标是攻占朴茨茅斯和查塔姆的海军造船厂并将其烧毁。

sentences.en: And that, they felt, would knock the British fleet out of the war.
sentences.zh: 他们觉得，这样就能把英国舰队打出战争。

sentences.en: And the British and French are now aiming to do the same.
sentences.zh: 现在英法联军的目标也是如此。

sentences.en: And so the plan is that you turn up, you do a kind of smash and grab raid, you destroy the Russian fleet, you burn its docks and job done.
sentences.zh: 所以计划是你们赶到那里，进行一次类似闪电突袭的行动，摧毁俄国舰队，烧毁它的造船厂，大功告成。

sentences.en: Brilliant.
sentences.zh: 太棒了。

sentences.en: You can go home.
sentences.zh: 你可以回家了。

sentences.en: Sounds very straightforward.
sentences.zh: 听起来非常直接。

sentences.en: Sounds easy.
sentences.zh: 听起来很简单。

sentences.en: Well, I mean, maybe it sounds straightforward, but there are a few probleMs.
sentences.zh: 好吧，我的意思是，也许听起来很简单，但有几个问题。

sentences.en: And the chief one is that there has been a complete lack of planning and the necessary logistics work has simply not been done.
sentences.zh: 其中最主要的是，这里完全缺乏规划，必要的后勤工作根本没有做好。

sentences.en: So I will give you a little list of all the things that the Allied High Command either aren't sure about or have got straight wrong.
sentences.zh: 所以我给你们列一个小清单，列出盟军最高指挥部要么拿不准、要么完全搞错的所有事情。

sentences.en: So they don't know how many troops the Russians have got and where they might be concentrated.
sentences.zh: 比如，他们不知道俄军有多少部队，也不知道他们可能集结在哪里。

sentences.en: How many of them are based in Sebastopol, for instance?
sentences.zh: 有多少人驻扎在塞瓦斯托波尔？

sentences.en: The geography of Crimea is something they only have a very vague sense of.
sentences.zh: 对克里米亚的地理情况，他们只有非常模糊的概念。

sentences.en: Their maps are not really cutting edge.
sentences.zh: 他们的地图可算不上什么最新科技。

sentences.en: The climate of Crimea, what's that like?
sentences.zh: 克里米亚的气候怎么样？

sentences.en: We're in September.
sentences.zh: 我们现在正处于九月。

sentences.en: One of the lessons of history is that it's unwise to invade Russia as autumn is approaching.
sentences.zh: 历史教训之一就是，在秋天临近时入侵俄国是不明智的。

sentences.en: But the Allies are ignoring this.
sentences.zh: 但盟军却忽视了这一点。

sentences.en: And that's because they've been reading travelogues, which claim that the winters in Crimea are very mild.
sentences.zh: 那是因为他们一直在阅读游记，游记声称克里米亚的冬天非常温和。

sentences.en: And so therefore, they assume there's no need for winter clothing.
sentences.zh: 因此，他们认为根本不需要冬衣。

sentences.en: And that if the worst comes to the worst and they can't find accommodation, which they haven't found, they can rely on their summer tents.
sentences.zh: 而且如果情况糟到极点，又找不到住处（而他们确实没找到），他们还可以依靠他们的夏用帐篷。

sentences.en: So that's part of it.
sentences.zh: 所以这只是其中一部分。

sentences.en: And I suppose even if the winters turn out to be bad, they're not planning to be there for the winter.
sentences.zh: 我想，即使冬天真的很糟糕，他们也没打算在那里过冬。

sentences.en: The plan is that they turn up, capture Sebastopol.
sentences.zh: 计划是他们赶到那里，攻占塞瓦斯托波尔。

sentences.en: I mean, how hard can it be?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，能有多难？

sentences.en: It'll be done in a week or so.
sentences.zh: 一个星期左右就能搞定。

sentences.en: Everything will be fine.
sentences.zh: 一切都会好起来的。

sentences.en: So they don't need to worry about how they would cope with a Russian winter.
sentences.zh: 所以他们根本不用担心如何应对俄国的冬天。

sentences.en: And then there's the issue of the defences of Sebastopol.
sentences.zh: 然后就是塞瓦斯托波尔的防御问题。

sentences.en: How many guns are defending it?
sentences.zh: 有多少门大炮在防守？

sentences.en: How many forts?
sentences.zh: 有多少座堡垒？

sentences.en: How high are the walls?
sentences.zh: 城墙有多高？

sentences.en: How many troops are stationed there?
sentences.zh: 有多少部队驻扎在那里？

sentences.en: How easy would it be to make a landing there?
sentences.zh: 在那里登陆会有多容易？

sentences.en: They don't know any of this.
sentences.zh: 这些他们全不知道。

sentences.en: I mean, these kinds of landings are really tricky, aren't they?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这种登陆真的很难，对吧？

sentences.en: Remember we did Nelson when Nelson was trying to capture, it was a Tenerife and he landed on Tenerife and it was a total disaster.
sentences.zh: 还记得我们讲纳尔逊的时候吗，当时纳尔逊试图去占领——那是特内里费岛，他在特内里费岛登陆，结果简直是一场灾难。

sentences.en: Amphibious landings in an age of like heavy guns are risky to say the least, aren't they?
sentences.zh: 在重炮时代的这种两栖登陆，保守点说也是充满风险的，对吧？

sentences.en: So presumably they have put a lot of thought into the landing and how this will work.
sentences.zh: 所以想必他们对登陆以及这该如何实施进行过深思熟虑。

sentences.en: And well, I mean, you're right.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我的意思是，你说得对。

sentences.en: They have memories of Tenerife and so they know that it is very, very dangerous to land under enemy guns.
sentences.zh: 他们还记着特内里费岛的教训，所以他们知道在敌人的炮火下登陆是非常非常危险的。

sentences.en: And because they don't know how many guns there are in Sebastopol, they decide it would be unwise to make a direct attack on their target.
sentences.zh: 正因为他们不知道塞瓦斯托波尔有多少门大炮，他们决定直接进攻目标是不明智的。

sentences.en: And so therefore they're going to have to find somewhere else to land.
sentences.zh: 因此他们必须找别的地方登陆。

sentences.en: So as you say, you'd think that that is something they would have worked out where they're going to make their landing.
sentences.zh: 所以正如你所说，你本会以为他们已经把要在哪里登陆这事给琢磨好了。

sentences.en: Dominic, they have not.
sentences.zh: 多米尼克，他们根本没有。

sentences.en: Oh, come on.
sentences.zh: 噢，拜托。

sentences.en: They are not Eisenhower.
sentences.zh: 他们可不是艾森豪威尔。

sentences.en: What can I say?
sentences.zh: 我还能说什么呢？

sentences.en: They're just kind of winging it basically.
sentences.zh: 他们基本上就是临场发挥。

sentences.en: And the reason why they haven't been able to decide on where they should land is that they'd sent a British officer to go and scope out the coast and he'd found a beach and
sentences.zh: 他们之所以一直无法决定在哪里登陆，是因为他们曾派出一名英国军官去侦察海岸，那人发现了一片海滩，

sentences.en: thought, oh, that looks perfect.
sentences.zh: 心想，哦，这看起来太完美了。

sentences.en: But it turns out that he's very short-sighted and that actually the beach is much, much narrower and shorter than they'd thought.
sentences.zh: 但事实证明，他是个高度近视，实际上那片海滩比他们想象的要窄得多、短得多。

sentences.en: And so therefore they are going to have to find somewhere else.
sentences.zh: 因此他们不得不另寻他处。

sentences.en: And madly, it's Raglan, the British commander in chief, who takes on the job.
sentences.zh: 疯狂的是，承担这项任务的竟然是英军总司令拉格兰。

sentences.en: So he's doing the reconnoitering.
sentences.zh: 所以是他亲自去侦察。

sentences.en: Yeah, with his one arm and his inability to climb up and down the side of a ship.
sentences.zh: 是的，带着他那条残臂，以及根本无法上下船舷的身体。

sentences.en: I mean, it's insane.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这太疯狂了。

sentences.en: So he somehow gets on board a steamship.
sentences.zh: 所以他不知怎么地登上了 一艘轮船。

sentences.en: I gather to probably pick him up and put him on board.
sentences.zh: 我猜大概是去接他并把他扶上船吧。

sentences.en: And he's escorted by the Agamemnon, which is this tremendous steamship with metal and everything.
sentences.zh: 护送他的是阿伽门农号，这是一艘装有金属护甲之类的庞大轮船。

sentences.en: Very exciting.
sentences.zh: 非常令人兴奋。

sentences.en: And so Raglan cruises off in his steamship ahead of the main fleet, and he starts going up and down the Crimean coast, looking for a suitable landing place.
sentences.zh: 于是拉格兰乘着他的轮船走在主力舰队前面，开始沿着克里米亚海岸上下巡视，寻找一个合适的登陆地点。

sentences.en: And they pass Sebastopol and so close that they can hear bells ringing from the churches of the city.
sentences.zh: 他们驶过塞瓦斯托波尔，离得如此之近，甚至能听到城中教堂传来的钟声。

sentences.en: And one of his staff on board Raglan's ship kind of touches his cap to a Russian officer on his horse.
sentences.zh: 拉格兰船上的一名随从人员向骑在马上的一个俄国军官礼貌地触了触军帽。

sentences.en: And the Russian officer taps his cap in return.
sentences.zh: 而那个俄国军官也回敬了一个军帽礼。

sentences.en: Oh, that's nice.
sentences.zh: 哦，那挺不错。

sentences.en: In return.
sentences.zh: 以礼相回。

sentences.en: And the kind of the chivalry of the moment.
sentences.zh: 这就是那个时刻的骑士精神吧。

sentences.en: But I think Raglan feels looking at the array of fortifications that Sebastopol has and the guns that are pointing out to see that their decision not to launch a surprise attack is
sentences.zh: 但我觉得拉格兰看着塞瓦斯托波尔那一排排防御工事以及指向海面的大炮，会觉得他们决定不发起突袭是

sentences.en: the right one, and that they made a good call there.
sentences.zh: 正确的选择，他们在那里做出了一个明智的决定。

sentences.en: And so they go north of Sebastopol.
sentences.zh: 于是他们来到了塞瓦斯托波尔以北。

sentences.en: And Raglan's eventual choice is a long stretch of beat, which lies south of a small port called
sentences.zh: 拉格兰最终选择的是一处长长的海滩，它位于一个叫

sentences.en: Eupatoria.
sentences.zh: 叶夫帕托里亚的小港口以南。

sentences.en: And I hadn't realized, but Eupatoria was named after Mithridates Eupator, who is the
sentences.zh: 我之前没意识到，叶夫帕托里亚是以米特拉达梯六世·欧帕托尔命名的，也就是那个

sentences.en: Mithridates who slaughtered all the Roman and Italian businessmen back in the age of
sentences.zh: 在苏拉时代屠杀所有罗马和意大利商人的

sentences.en: Sulla.
sentences.zh: 米特拉达梯。

sentences.en: Oh, yeah.
sentences.zh: 哦，对。

sentences.en: And the Sulla, Maris and Sulla series.
sentences.zh: 还有苏拉、马略和苏拉系列。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: So there's a little link there.
sentences.zh: 所以这里还有个小小的联系。

sentences.en: Amazing.
sentences.zh: 太神奇了。

sentences.en: So the pros of landing at this beach south of Eupatoria is that it's undefended.
sentences.zh: 在叶夫帕托里亚以南的这片海滩登陆的好处是，这里没有防御。

sentences.en: The Russians don't think anyone will be landing there.
sentences.zh: 俄国人根本没想到会有人在这里登陆。

sentences.en: And it's flanked on either side by salt marshes.
sentences.zh: 而且它两侧都有盐沼夹道。

sentences.en: So that means that it's able, you know, it's much easier to secure it as a landing place.
sentences.zh: 这意味着你可以（你知道的），作为登陆地点要安全得多。

sentences.en: The cons are that it's 40 miles north of Sebastopol.
sentences.zh: 坏处是它在塞瓦斯托波尔以北40英里处。

sentences.en: So there is no prospect of taking the Russians by surprise at all if they go there.
sentences.zh: 所以如果他们去那里，就完全没有出其不意袭击俄国人的可能了。

sentences.en: And also, its name is slightly ominous because it's called Calamita.
sentences.zh: 而且，它的名字有点不祥，因为它叫卡拉米塔（Calamita）。

sentences.en: And so the British inevitably start calling it Calamity Bay.
sentences.zh: 于是英国人不可避免地开始把它叫做灾难湾（Calamity Bay）。

sentences.en: And there's a further ominous portent, which is that when the Allied fleet drops anchor in
sentences.zh: 还有一个更不祥的预兆，那就是当盟军舰队在

sentences.en: Calamita Bay and start unloading, it's the 14th of September.
sentences.zh: 卡拉米塔湾抛锚并开始卸货时，正好是9月14日。

sentences.en: And that is the anniversary of Napoleon's entry into Moscow.
sentences.zh: 那正是拿破仑进入莫斯科的纪念日。

sentences.en: Oh.
sentences.zh: 噢。

sentences.en: That didn't go well.
sentences.zh: 那次可没进行顺利。

sentences.en: So the French let themselves down in the retreat from Moscow.
sentences.zh: 所以法国人在从莫斯科撤退时丢了面子。

sentences.en: But on this occasion, they actually, they perform splendid, don't they?
sentences.zh: 但这一次，他们实际上表现得十分出色，对吧？

sentences.en: Put up a good show.
sentences.zh: 表现得很不错。

sentences.en: Very smooth, very efficient, their landing.
sentences.zh: 他们的登陆非常顺利、非常高效。

sentences.en: And there are no Russians there.
sentences.zh: 而且那里没有俄国人。

sentences.en: Or rather, there's only one Russian there to confront them.
sentences.zh: 或者更准确地说，只有一个俄国人在那里等着他们。

sentences.en: It's a local customs officer.
sentences.zh: 那是一个当地的海关官员。

sentences.en: And he rides down and demands that they go into quarantine.
sentences.zh: 他骑马赶来，要求他们接受检疫隔离。

sentences.en: I love that.
sentences.zh: 我太喜欢这个了。

sentences.en: And I can entirely understand why he would do that because, you know, they're all ridden with cholerae and dysentra.
sentences.zh: 而且我完全理解他为什么要这么做，因为（你知道的）他们全都满身霍乱和痢疾。

sentences.en: So they probably should do.
sentences.zh: 所以他们大概真的应该隔离一下。

sentences.en: But the French ignore this and say they're not going to quarantine.
sentences.zh: 但法国人无视了这一点，说他们绝不接受隔离。

sentences.en: So what about our brave boys, Dominic?
sentences.zh: 那我们的英勇小伙子们呢，多米尼克？

sentences.en: Yeah, surely we are notable for our military efficiency.
sentences.zh: 对啊，我们难道不以军事效率著称吗？

sentences.en: We're not.
sentences.zh: 我们并不是。

sentences.en: Well, no.
sentences.zh: 好吧，并没有。

sentences.en: I'm afraid to say that we are a total shambles.
sentences.zh: 我恐慌地（不得不）说，我们简直是一团糟。

sentences.en: So we have no carts with which to offload the baggage, unlike the French.
sentences.zh: 所以我们没有像法国人那样用来卸载行李的马车。

sentences.en: They start unloading the horses and the wind whips up the surf and the horses get frightened by it.
sentences.zh: 他们开始卸载马匹，风卷起海浪，马匹因此受到了惊吓。

sentences.en: So that takes a long time.
sentences.zh: 所以这花了很长时间。

sentences.en: And they've got all these tents and it takes them days and days to unload it.
sentences.zh: 他们有那么多的帐篷，花了整整好几天才卸载完。

sentences.en: And I'm afraid that Saint-Arnaud, who's been stretched off his boat and installed in a chair, deck chair on the beach, he's watching this.
sentences.zh: 恐怕圣阿尔诺（他刚从船上被抬下来，安顿在海滩上的一把折叠椅里）正看着这一切。

sentences.en: And he's very withering.
sentences.zh: 他对此冷嘲热讽。

sentences.en: He says, the English has the unpleasant habit of always being late.
sentences.zh: 他说：“英国人有个令人讨厌的习惯，那就是总是迟到。”

sentences.en: He's a sick man, though.
sentences.zh: 不过他是个病人就是了。

sentences.en: So you can forgive him for making...
sentences.zh: 所以你可以原谅他说出……

sentences.en: I know, raving.
sentences.zh: 我知道，简直胡言乱语。

sentences.en: Madness.
sentences.zh: 太疯狂了。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对啊。

sentences.en: But I mean, he actually...
sentences.zh: 但我的意思是，他实际上……

sentences.en: I mean, it's not madness because he's right.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是这并非疯狂，因为他是对的。

sentences.en: It takes the British five days.
sentences.zh: 英国人花了整整五天时间。

sentences.en: It's taken the French one day.
sentences.zh: 法国人只用了一天。

sentences.en: It takes the British five days.
sentences.zh: 英国人却花了五天。

sentences.en: And so there's a whole load of kind of general disembarkation shenanigans.
sentences.zh: 于是发生了一大堆各种各样的大规模卸货闹剧。

sentences.en: But finally, the British are ready and the march on Sebastopol begins.
sentences.zh: 但最终，英国人准备就绪，进军塞瓦斯托波尔开始了。

sentences.en: And it looks amazing.
sentences.zh: 而且看起来极其壮观。

sentences.en: It makes an incredible spectacle.
sentences.zh: 这构成了一场令人难以置信的视觉盛宴。

sentences.en: 60,000 men marching in double columns.
sentences.zh: 六万大军排成双纵队行进。

sentences.en: You've got the French in their blue uniforms, the British in their red.
sentences.zh: 你看法军穿着蓝色的制服，英军穿着红色的制服。

sentences.en: You've got bands playing, you've got colors flying, everyone full of excitement.
sentences.zh: 乐队在演奏，军旗在飘扬，每个人都兴奋不已。

sentences.en: But we've mentioned how disease-ridden these armies are.
sentences.zh: 但我们刚才提到了，这些军队是多么的疾病肆虐。

sentences.en: There's a sense in which the show of energy and dazzle is a bit deceptive.
sentences.zh: 某种意义上，这种充满活力和耀眼的展示其实有点虚幻。

sentences.en: And as the armies go, there are men who are just dropping out and, you know,
sentences.zh: 随着大军行进，不断有人掉队，你知道的，

sentences.en: clutching their stomachs and doubling up and voiding their bowels and just lying there and refusing to get up, even though they must be nervous of the Cossacks.
sentences.zh: 他们捂着肚子、痛苦弯腰、腹泻不止，就那样倒在地上拒绝起身，尽管他们肯定对哥萨克人感到紧张。

sentences.en: Gradually, as the hours pass, the sense of enthusiasm starts to fade and the bands stop playing and there's no cheering.
sentences.zh: 渐渐地，随着时间流逝，那种狂热的情绪开始消退，乐队停止了演奏，也没有了欢呼声。

sentences.en: I mean, is this like you and your walk around the coast of Wales?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这就像你和你在威尔士海岸徒步那样吗？

sentences.en: So like it.
sentences.zh: 太像了。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: You head off full of enthusiasm and after about half an hour, you'll say, oh, let's go to the pub.
sentences.zh: 你满腔热情地出发，大约半小时后，你就会说，哦，咱们去酒吧吧。

sentences.en: And there's probably less cholera.
sentences.zh: 而且霍乱可能没那么多。

sentences.en: That's good to hear.
sentences.zh: 听到这个真高兴。

sentences.en: And it's really brutal because there's no water.
sentences.zh: 而且这真的很残酷，因为没有水。

sentences.en: It's really hot.
sentences.zh: 天气真的很热。

sentences.en: We've said the horses, you know, they've been on these terrible rides with cardigan and things.
sentences.zh: 我们说过，那些马，你知道的，它们跟着卡迪根他们经历了可怕的行军。

sentences.en: So they're not in the best condition.
sentences.zh: 所以它们的状态并不是最好的。

sentences.en: But the Russians have not seized their chance to drive them into the sea.
sentences.zh: 但俄国人并没有抓住机会把他们赶进海里。

sentences.en: No, because they are luring them onwards.
sentences.zh: 没有，因为他们在诱敌深入。

sentences.en: Oh, of course they're cunning.
sentences.zh: 哦，他们当然很狡猾。

sentences.en: And so I think the British and the French are aware of this.
sentences.zh: 所以我想英法联军也意识到了这一点。

sentences.en: And so the silence comes to seem very sinister.
sentences.zh: 因此，这种沉默开始显得非常诡异。

sentences.en: And then they start to observe the occasional Cossack horseman on the horizon and he'll sit there on his saddle and then wheel and vanish.
sentences.zh: 接着，他们开始发现在地平线上出现零星的哥萨克骑兵，他在马鞍上坐一会儿，然后调转马头消失了。

sentences.en: Oh, God, this is very Custer vibes, don't you think?
sentences.zh: 哦，天哪，这很有卡斯特将军的感觉，你不觉得吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, and it's massive Napoleon's invasion of Russia vibes as well, more germainly.
sentences.zh: 对，而且更贴切地说，这非常有拿破仑入侵俄国时的宏大既视感。

sentences.en: I mean, that must be what the French are thinking.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，法军心里肯定也是这么想的。

sentences.en: And so they start asking themselves, where are the Russians?
sentences.zh: 于是他们开始自问，俄国人在哪里？

sentences.en: And the sun rises in the sky and the army grows more and more thirsty.
sentences.zh: 太阳在空中升起，军队变得越来越口渴。

sentences.en: And I think the kind of, you know, the emptiness of this great glittering plane ahead of them just comes to seem more and more ominous,
sentences.zh: 而且我认为，你知道的，他们面前那片广阔闪耀的平原上的那种空旷感，开始显得越来越不祥，

sentences.en: it's more and more pregnant with a danger that they suspect is lurking beyond the kind of the ridges that they can see stretching away from them.
sentences.zh: 它越来越孕育着一种危险，他们怀疑这种危险正潜伏在他们能看到的那些延伸出去的山脊后面。

sentences.en: Now, Raglan could, of course, have scouted these approaches out because he does have the Light Brigade.
sentences.zh: 当然，拉格兰本可以侦察这些行军路线，因为他确实拥有轻骑兵旅。

sentences.en: That's their job.
sentences.zh: 那是他们的工作。

sentences.en: It's to go and reconnoiter.
sentences.zh: 他们的职责就是去进行侦察。

sentences.en: But he's not prepared to slip the leash to allow the Light Brigade to go and do their job.
sentences.zh: 但他并不准备放开绳索，让轻骑兵旅去执行他们的任务。

sentences.en: And so people may be wondering, well, why not?
sentences.zh: 所以人们可能会想，为什么不呢？

sentences.en: And the answer is, as we've said, the horses are in a terrible state and Raglan wants them restored to health as soon as possible.
sentences.zh: 答案正如我们所说，马匹状况糟糕，拉格兰希望它们尽快恢复健康。

sentences.en: But also the cavalry, men as well as horses,
sentences.zh: 但同时，骑兵们，包括人和马，

sentences.en: have been so diminished by the various kind of diseases and plagues that have been rife in Bulgaria that Raglan fears that there aren't enough of them to be effective in combat,
sentences.zh: 都在保加利亚肆虐的各种疾病和瘟疫中元气大伤，以至于拉格兰担心，如果遭到哥萨克人或其他敌人的袭击，他们的人数根本不足以在战斗中发挥有效作用。

sentences.en: should they be attacked by the Cossacks or whatever.
sentences.zh: 如果遭到哥萨克人或什么人的袭击。

sentences.en: And so he makes a joke of it and says that his intention is to keep the cavalry in a band box.
sentences.zh: 因此他开玩笑说，他的意图是要把骑兵放在一个精致的帽盒里保护起来。

sentences.en: And a band box is kind of like a hat box or something that a lady would keep her muff in.
sentences.zh: 而帽盒有点像帽子盒，或者是贵妇人用来放防寒手笼的那种东西。

sentences.en: So it's meant as a joke, but it's a joke that is going to misfire very badly over the course of the next few days.
sentences.zh: 所以这本来是个玩笑，但在接下来的几天里，这个玩笑却会产生非常糟糕的后果。

sentences.en: And, of course, Lord Cardigan doesn't find it funny at all because he is massively frustrated.
sentences.zh: 当然，卡迪根勋爵一点也觉得不好笑，因为他感到了极大的挫败感。

sentences.en: He's dying to sweep ahead Custer style and reconnoiter some Cossacks.
sentences.zh: 他渴望像卡斯特那样一路横扫并侦察一些哥萨克人。

sentences.en: So Cardigan and the Light Brigade are still cutting a dash, are they?
sentences.zh: 所以卡迪根和轻骑兵旅仍然出尽了风头，是吗？

sentences.en: Because last time you emphasised their amazing outfits.
sentences.zh: 因为上次你强调了他们惊艳的行头。

sentences.en: Oh, they look amazing.
sentences.zh: 哦，他们看起来棒极了。

sentences.en: Yeah, they look amazing.
sentences.zh: 对，他们看起来帅呆了。

sentences.en: Even though they've been soiled by dysentery or whatever, they still look absolutely splendid.
sentences.zh: 尽管他们的衣服可能被痢疾或其他东西弄脏了，但他们看起来依然绝对光彩照人。

sentences.en: Well, remember, Lord Lucan had been sorting out the laundry women very precisely to be as efficient as possible.
sentences.zh: 好吧，记住，卢肯勋爵曾非常精确地整顿过洗衣妇，以确保尽可能的高效。

sentences.en: So even though they may have soiled their cherry pants, these cherry pants have been freshly laundered.
sentences.zh: 所以即使他们的樱桃红裤子弄脏了，这些裤子也已经被重新洗干净了。

sentences.en: So we're looking magnificent.
sentences.zh: 所以我们看起来威风凛凛。

sentences.en: Brilliant.
sentences.zh: 太棒了。

sentences.en: And they've got their gold frogging on their blue jackets.
sentences.zh: 他们的蓝色夹克上绣着金色的花边编绳。

sentences.en: They've got their furred polices.
sentences.zh: 他们穿着镶着毛皮的轻骑兵短外套。

sentences.en: They look amazing.
sentences.zh: 他们看起来帅呆了。

sentences.en: And they are riding at the head of the army.
sentences.zh: 而且他们骑在军队的最前端。

sentences.en: So they're kind of screening the army.
sentences.zh: 所以他们实际上是在为军队做掩护侦察。

sentences.en: And Lord Cardigan is at the head of Light Brigade.
sentences.zh: 卡迪根勋爵担任轻骑兵旅的指挥官。

sentences.en: So on that level, it's great.
sentences.zh: 从这个层面来看，这很棒。

sentences.en: But he wants to be roaming across the plains.
sentences.zh: 但他想要在平原上纵横驰骋。

sentences.en: And he hates this feeling of being tied to Lord Raglan's apron strings.
sentences.zh: 而且他讨厌这种被束缚在拉格兰勋爵围裙带上的感觉。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So that's bad enough.
sentences.zh: 所以这已经够糟糕的了。

sentences.en: But there's something even worse, which is that he is now having to answer for literally everything he does to Lord Lucan.
sentences.zh: 但还有更糟的事情，那就是他现在必须对卢肯勋爵汇报他所做的字面意义上的每一件事。

sentences.en: Oh, his brother-in-law.
sentences.zh: 哦，他的连襟。

sentences.en: His brother-in-law, who he hates.
sentences.zh: 他的连襟，也是他痛恨的人。

sentences.en: And Lord Lucan is just a massive micromanager.
sentences.zh: 而且卢肯勋爵简直是个极端的微观管理者。

sentences.en: And he is determined never to let Cardigan go rogue again.
sentences.zh: 他下定决心绝不再让卡迪根独自胡来。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And I think he's enjoying asserting his authority over this brother-in-law, whom he absolutely detests.
sentences.zh: 而且我想他很享受在这个他绝对痛恨的连襟面前确立自己的权威。

sentences.en: And so to this end, he's placed a member of his own staff by the side of Cardigan, obviously with the aim of keeping watch on him.
sentences.zh: 为此，他在卡迪根身边安插了自己参谋部的一名成员，显然目的是监视他。

sentences.en: And so Cardigan, unsurprisingly, views this guy as a spy.
sentences.zh: 因此，毫无意外地，卡迪根把这家伙视作间谍。

sentences.en: So there's massive resentment.
sentences.zh: 所以存在着巨大的怨恨。

sentences.en: And they're constantly kind of snapping at each other.
sentences.zh: 他们总是互相针锋相对、挑刺。

sentences.en: And actually, one of the officers in the Light Brigade describes the two brothers-in-law as like a pair of scissors who go snip and snip and snip without doing each other any harm.
sentences.zh: 事实上，轻骑兵旅的一名军官将这两个连襟形容为一把剪刀，咔嚓、咔嚓、咔嚓地剪个不停，却又伤不到对方分毫。

sentences.en: But God help the poor devil who gets between them.
sentences.zh: 但愿上帝保佑那些夹在他们中间的可怜虫。

sentences.en: They're just never, you know, they're never stopping.
sentences.zh: 他们就是从不，你知道的，从不罢休。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So they're just bickering away and then suddenly, abruptly, there is a taste of action at laSt.
sentences.zh: 所以他们一直在争吵，然后突然之间，激战的气息终于降临了。

sentences.en: Because at 2 p.m., and they've been marching by this point for 12 miles, the Allies reach their first river.
sentences.zh: 因为在下午2点，此时他们已经行军了12英里，盟军到达了他们的第一条河流。

sentences.en: And this is a river called the Bulganek.
sentences.zh: 这是一条名为布尔加内克的河流。

sentences.en: So it's the first opportunity to drink amid this terrible stifling heat.
sentences.zh: 所以在这种可怕的闷热中，这是他们第一次有机会喝水。

sentences.en: And so the infantry, they pretty much abandon discipline and start scrabbling down the side of the slopes, down the valley to get the water, scooping the water up,
sentences.zh: 于是步兵们几乎放弃了纪律，开始争先恐后地顺着山坡、沿着山谷冲下去找水，用手捧起水，

sentences.en: slacking their thirSt.
sentences.zh: 解解他们的干渴。

sentences.en: And while they're doing this, Cardigan is instructed by Lord Raglan to cross the river, to go up the slope of the valley beyond and to reconnoiter it.
sentences.zh: 正当他们这么做的时候，拉格兰勋爵指示卡迪根过河，登上前方山谷的山坡去进行侦察。

sentences.en: And so Cardigan is delighted at this.
sentences.zh: 卡迪根对此感到高兴极了。

sentences.en: And he gives his men the order.
sentences.zh: 他向手下下达了命令。

sentences.en: And they're about to set off when who should come riding up but Lord Lucan,
sentences.zh: 正当他们准备出发时，谁骑马赶来了呢——正是卢肯勋爵，

sentences.en: who very coolly announces that he is taking charge and replacing Lord Cardigan at the head of the Light Brigade.
sentences.zh: 他非常冷酷地宣布由他接管指挥权，并替换掉轻骑兵旅长卡迪根勋爵。

sentences.en: Oh.
sentences.zh: 哦。

sentences.en: So Cardigan is steaming, but he has to suck it up because Lucan is his superior officer.
sentences.zh: 所以卡迪根气得七窍生烟，但他不得不忍气吞声，因为卢肯是他的上级军官。

sentences.en: And so the Light Brigade cross the river and they advance up this slope on the far side and there's a ridge ahead of them.
sentences.zh: 于是轻骑兵旅过河，向对岸的山坡推进，前方有一道山脊。

sentences.en: They can't see what's beyond the ridge.
sentences.zh: 他们看不到山脊后面是什么。

sentences.en: And so they breast this ridge and there ahead of them, they see a body of some 2,000 Cossacks.
sentences.zh: 当他们翻过这道山脊时，赫然发现前方有一支大约2000人的哥萨克部队。

sentences.en: So they are outnumbered at least two to one.
sentences.zh: 所以他们在人数上处于至少二对一的劣势。

sentences.en: The Light Brigade are outnumbered.
sentences.zh: 轻骑兵旅处于劣势。

sentences.en: Yeah, the Light Brigade is outnumbered.
sentences.zh: 是的，轻骑兵旅寡不敌众。

sentences.en: But who cares?
sentences.zh: 但这有什么关系？

sentences.en: You know, this is a chance for action.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，这是大显身手的好机会。

sentences.en: So huzzah.
sentences.zh: 所以，乌拉。

sentences.en: So Cardigan says, you know, line up and they do this with beautiful precision.
sentences.zh: 于是卡迪根说，排好队，他们以极度精准的动作完成了列队。

sentences.en: You know, Cardigan's been trained to do this for years and years.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，卡迪根为此进行了年复一年的训练。

sentences.en: But Lucan, who's been watching it, announces that he's not satisfied with the order and the ranking that Cardigan has told them to take up.
sentences.zh: 但一直在旁观看的卢肯却宣布，他对卡迪根下令摆出的队列和阵型很不满意。

sentences.en: And so he starts correcting the order of the troops, even though there's a massive great load of Cossacks kind of itching for action ahead of them.
sentences.zh: 于是他开始纠正部队的队形，尽管他们前方正有一大群跃跃欲试的哥萨克人。

sentences.en: And he's fussing over them and shouting at Cardigan for having got it wrong.
sentences.zh: 他在那里大惊小怪，并因为卡迪根弄错了而冲他大喊大叫。

sentences.en: And Cardigan shouts back at him.
sentences.zh: 卡迪根也冲他大吼回去。

sentences.en: And they end up having this massive stand-up row.
sentences.zh: 结果他们爆发了一场激烈的当面争吵。

sentences.en: And all the time the Cossacks are closing in.
sentences.zh: 而与此同时，哥萨克人正在步步逼近。

sentences.en: And then they start firing at the Light Brigade.
sentences.zh: 接着他们开始向轻骑兵旅开火。

sentences.en: And the two guys are still having this kind of stand-up row.
sentences.zh: 而这两个家伙还在进行这种当面争吵。

sentences.en: And an order comes to them from Raglan that instead of confronting the Cossacks, they are to withdraw.
sentences.zh: 这时拉格兰传来了命令，要求他们不要与哥萨克人正面交锋，而是立刻撤退。

sentences.en: And Cardigan can't believe it.
sentences.zh: 卡迪根简直不敢相信。

sentences.en: The Cossacks are advancing on them.
sentences.zh: 哥萨克人正向他们推进。

sentences.en: They've got a retreat in front of the Cossacks.
sentences.zh: 他们竟然得在哥萨克人面前撤退。

sentences.en: Absolutely outrageous.
sentences.zh: 简直是奇耻大辱。

sentences.en: But Lucan accepts that this is an authentic order from Raglan.
sentences.zh: 但卢肯接受了这是来自拉格兰的真实命令。

sentences.en: And so he gives the command to the Light Brigade to retreat.
sentences.zh: 于是他向轻骑兵旅下达了撤退的命令。

sentences.en: And the Cossacks, seeing the Light Brigade retreat, boo and jeer them.
sentences.zh: 哥萨克人看到轻骑兵旅撤退，纷纷发出嘘声和嘲笑。

sentences.en: And they're firing at them.
sentences.zh: 并且向他们开火。

sentences.en: And by now they're in range.
sentences.zh: 此时他们已经进入了射程。

sentences.en: And a couple of the 13th Light Dragoons get hit in the leg.
sentences.zh: 第13轻骑兵龙骑兵团的几名士兵腿部中弹。

sentences.en: And thereby become the first casualties of the Crimean War.
sentences.zh: 并因此成为了克里米亚战争的第一批伤亡人员。

sentences.en: And one of these troopers rides up to his commanding officer.
sentences.zh: 其中一名骑兵骑马来到他的指挥官面前。

sentences.en: And he's literally holding his leg in his arm.
sentences.zh: 他手里竟然抱着自己的那条腿。

sentences.en: It's been kind of blown off.
sentences.zh: 那条腿差不多已经被炸断了。

sentences.en: And he requests permission to fall out, which is granted.
sentences.zh: 他请求离队，并得到了批准。

sentences.en: Oh, that's great.
sentences.zh: 哦，太棒了。

sentences.en: So tremendous British pluck.
sentences.zh: 这展现了惊人的英国人硬气。

sentences.en: And the other one ends up being evacuated to England and is presented with a wooden leg.
sentences.zh: 另一个家伙最终被撤退送到英国，并获赠了一条木腿。

sentences.en: Or to be more accurate, a leg made out of cork.
sentences.zh: 或者更准确地说，是一条软木做成的假腿。

sentences.en: Cork leg.
sentences.zh: 软木腿。

sentences.en: A cork leg.
sentences.zh: 一条软木腿。

sentences.en: So that's good.
sentences.zh: 这倒挺好。

sentences.en: So did Raglan tell them to fall back because they're outnumbered?
sentences.zh: 那么拉格兰是因为他们寡不敌众才让他们撤回来的吗？

sentences.en: And because he could see the commanders were fighting among themselves?
sentences.zh: 而且因为他看出指挥官们在内讧？

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 不是。

sentences.en: Oh.
sentences.zh: 哦。

sentences.en: So he has ridden to high ground and looked out over the river.
sentences.zh: 原来他骑马上了高地，俯瞰着整条河流。

sentences.en: And he can see that there's a kind of another ridge ahead of them.
sentences.zh: 他能看到他们前方还有另一道山脊。

sentences.en: And that beyond this ridge, there is a massive amount of Russian infantry and artillery.
sentences.zh: 在这道山脊后面，有数量庞大的俄国步兵和炮兵。

sentences.en: So effectively, had the Light Brigade not withdrawn, they would probably have been wiped out.
sentences.zh: 所以实际上，如果轻骑兵旅没有撤退，他们很可能会全军覆没。

sentences.en: So it was the correct order to be given.
sentences.zh: 因此这是一个正确的命令。

sentences.en: But this isn't at all how the Light Brigade themselves see it.
sentences.zh: 但这可完全不是轻骑兵旅自己眼中的情况。

sentences.en: They feel completely humiliated because they've been humiliated in front of the Russians, but also in front of their own infantry, who are very prone to seeing them as show ponies.
sentences.zh: 他们感到彻底受辱，因为他们不仅在俄国人面前丢了脸，还在他们自己的步兵面前丢了脸，而步兵们本来就很倾向于把他们看作花架子骑兵。

sentences.en: You know, kind of toffs on horses.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，就是骑着马的阔少爷们。

sentences.en: And so they feel really, you know, really mortified and ashamed by the whole business.
sentences.zh: 所以整件事让他们感到无比的羞辱和难堪。

sentences.en: And they don't blame Raglan, they blame Lord Lucan.
sentences.zh: 而且他们不怪拉格伦，他们怪卢肯勋爵。

sentences.en: They say that it's his fault.
sentences.zh: 他们说这是他的错。

sentences.en: And a very harsh name is coined for him, Lord Lucan.
sentences.zh: 人们给他起了一个非常刺耳的外号，卢肯勋爵。

sentences.en: And this is adopted across the cavalry and then across the army.
sentences.zh: 这个外号在骑兵中传开，接着在整个军队中传开。

sentences.en: And it's really unfair on Lucan.
sentences.zh: 这对卢肯来说实在很不公平。

sentences.en: It's really unfair.
sentences.zh: 真的太不公平了。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: He wanted to have a go at the Gossacks, but it was Raglan who ordered them.
sentences.zh: 他本想去跟哥萨克人较量一番，但下令的是拉格伦。

sentences.en: Well, although Raglan did the right thing.
sentences.zh: 嗯，尽管拉格伦做对了事。

sentences.en: Raglan does the right thing, but Lucan gets the blame for it.
sentences.zh: 拉格伦做对了事，但背锅的却是卢肯。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: And it's called Lord Lucan.
sentences.zh: 然后这就成了卢肯勋爵的代名词。

sentences.en: So it's terrible for him.
sentences.zh: 所以这对他来说太糟糕了。

sentences.en: And so it's a very inglorious first taste of action for the Light Brigade.
sentences.zh: 因此，轻骑兵旅的初次实战可以说是毫无荣耀可言。

sentences.en: But I guess their only consolation is, well, we are going to have chance for some action tomorrow.
sentences.zh: 但我猜他们唯一的慰藉就是，好吧，明天我们还有机会大干一场。

sentences.en: Because that night they're bivouacked by the side of this river, the Bulganek.
sentences.zh: 因为那天晚上他们在布尔加内克河畔露营。

sentences.en: And they can see about six miles to the south, there's this great blaze of watch fires.
sentences.zh: 他们可以看到南边大约六英里处，有一片巨大的篝火在闪耀。

sentences.en: And these fires mark the camp of the Russian army.
sentences.zh: 这些篝火标志着俄军的营地。

sentences.en: And the Russian army has taken up a very formidable defensive position on the heights that rise above a river called the Alma.
sentences.zh: 俄军在阿尔马河上方的高地上占据了一个非常强大的防御阵地。

sentences.en: And these heights are so formidable that, in fact, the Russian high command is completely confident of victory.
sentences.zh: 这些高地是如此险要，以至于俄军最高指挥部对胜利信心十足。

sentences.en: They think that the allies have no chance.
sentences.zh: 他们认为盟军毫无胜算。

sentences.en: And so dawn comes.
sentences.zh: 于是黎明到来。

sentences.en: As the Allied columns begin advancing towards the Alma, they're being shadowed by bands of Cossacks.
sentences.zh: 当盟军纵队开始向阿尔马河推进时，他们遭到了成群的哥萨克人的尾随监视。

sentences.en: Plumes of smoke are arising from farms and hamlets that are being torched by the Russian forces to deny the Allies any supplies.
sentences.zh: 农场和村庄腾起缕缕浓烟，这些地方被俄军纵火焚烧，以剥夺盟军的任何补给。

sentences.en: And as the Allies approach the heights of the Alma, on these heights above the river, a party of 30 young ladies from Sebastopol are settling down for a picnic.
sentences.zh: 正当盟军接近阿尔马高地时，在河上方的高地上，来自塞瓦斯托波尔的30名年轻淑女正安顿下来准备野餐。

sentences.zh: 这些是俄国指挥官缅希科夫亲王的私人客宾。

sentences.en: And they've been invited by Prince Menchikov to witness the inevitable annihilation of the British and the French.
sentences.zh: 她们应缅希科夫亲王的邀请，前来见证英法联军不可避免的彻底覆灭。

sentences.en: Oh, my words.
sentences.zh: 天哪。

sentences.en: But, Dominic, the big question.
sentences.zh: 但是，多米尼克，最大的问题来了。

sentences.en: Are the French and the British doomed to annihilation?
sentences.zh: 法军和英军注定要全军覆没吗？

sentences.zh: 还是英国的坚韧与法国的干劲胜出？

sentences.zh: 他们能赢得这场胜利吗？

sentences.en: Oh, gosh.
sentences.zh: 噢，天哪。

sentences.en: A party of 30 young ladies, who are the guests of the Russian commander, Prince Menshikov, have installed themselves on their blankets.
sentences.zh: 30位年轻淑女，作为俄国指挥官缅希科夫亲王的客人，已经在她们的毛毯上坐好了。

sentences.en: They've got out their caviar and smoked salmon and their blinis or whatever they're having.
sentences.zh: 她们拿出了鱼子酱、熏三文鱼和俄式薄饼或者她们正在吃的其他东西。

sentences.en: They're looking forward to watching their brave Russian boys inflict a stinging defeat on the British and French invaders who have dared to set foot on the sacred soil of the Crimean Peninsula.
sentences.zh: 她们正期待着看着她们勇敢的俄国小伙子们给英法侵略者以沉重的打击，这些侵略者竟然敢踏上克里米亚半岛这片神圣的土地。

sentences.en: And, to begin with, these ladies have a lovely time, don't they?
sentences.zh: 起初，这些女士们度过了一段美好的时光，不是吗？

sentences.en: So, they have a wonderful view.
sentences.zh: 所以，她们拥有极佳的视野。

sentences.en: They can see the British and the French sort of trudging along beneath them.
sentences.zh: 她们可以看到英法联军在她们下方艰难跋涉。

sentences.en: The British are in their fancy uniforms, aren't they?
sentences.zh: 英国人穿着华丽的制服，对吧？

sentences.en: But there's loads and loads of infantry.
sentences.zh: 但有许许多多的步兵。

sentences.en: And, actually, to start with, the ladies think, well, these foreigners are actually quite brave.
sentences.zh: 其实，一开始，女士们觉得，这些外国人其实挺勇敢的。

sentences.en: They're doing quite well.
sentences.zh: 他们表现得相当不错。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: I think they enjoy the spectacle.
sentences.zh: 我想她们很享受这种奇观。

sentences.en: Something of watching a rugby match, I imagine.
sentences.zh: 我想这有点像观看橄榄球比赛。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: The soldiers are very brave, very manly.
sentences.zh: 士兵们非常勇敢，极具男子气概。

sentences.en: They have, as you said, absolutely splendid uniforMs.
sentences.zh: 正如你所说，他们穿着绝对光鲜亮丽的制服。

sentences.en: Much more handsome, I think, the ladies feel than the uniforms of their own boys, which are slightly grey and drab.
sentences.zh: 女士们觉得，比起她们自己小伙子们略显灰暗单调的制服，这些制服要帅气得多。

sentences.en: You know, the French are bright blue, the British are bright red.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，法国人是亮蓝色，英国人是亮红色。

sentences.en: So, I think they do enjoy the spectacle.
sentences.zh: 所以，我想她们确实很享受这个奇观。

sentences.en: But then, as the day advances, I think they start to find their enjoyment fraying.
sentences.zh: 但随后，随着一天的推移，我想她们开始觉得这种乐趣在消磨。

sentences.en: It doesn't seem to be going quite as well as Prince Metchikoff had assured them that it would.
sentences.zh: 情况似乎并不像缅希科夫亲王向她们保证的那样顺利。

sentences.en: And, finally, in the middle of the afternoon, they are approached by a very grim-faced Russian officer who tells them, and I quote,
sentences.zh: 最后，在下午过半时，一个面色严峻的俄国军官走近她们，告诉她们，我引用原话：

sentences.en: they must fly for their lives in their carriages, and the quote comes from the report of William Russell, the Times correspondent,
sentences.zh: 她们必须坐马车夺路逃命，这段引文出自《泰晤士报》记者威廉·拉塞尔的报道，

sentences.en: who ended up and inspected the remains of their picnic because they'd left in such a hurry that they'd left all their blinis and their champagne and whatnot.
sentences.zh: 他最终去查看了她们野餐的遗迹，因为她们走得太匆忙，把所有的俄式薄饼、香槟之类都留下了。

sentences.en: And they're taken away.
sentences.zh: 然后她们被带走了。

sentences.en: And these ladies are the first Russians to beat a retreat from what was supposed to be an absolutely impregnable position.
sentences.zh: 这些女士是第一批从本应坚不可摧的阵地上狼狈撤退的俄国人。

sentences.en: But, Dominic, they are not going to be the last because many more Russians are going to be forced into retreat.
sentences.zh: 但是，多米尼克，她们不会是最后一批，因为会有更多的俄国人被迫撤退。

sentences.en: And, in fact, by the end of the day, the entire Russian army will be hurtling as fast as they can away from the heights of the Alma, back towards Sebastopol and beyond.
sentences.zh: 事实上，到了一天结束时，整个俄国军队将以最快的速度从阿尔马高地仓皇逃离，退回塞瓦斯托波尔及更远的地方。

sentences.en: So, the result of the day has made a bitter mockery of the overconfidence of the Russian prince.
sentences.zh: 因此，这一天的结果无情地嘲弄了俄国亲王的盲目自信。

sentences.en: And so, this is a resounding victory, is it, for the far-sighted leadership and decisive generalship of the British and French commanders, or am I mistaken?
sentences.zh: 所以，对于英法指挥官深谋远虑的领导和果断的将帅之才来说，这是一场辉煌的胜利，还是我弄错了？

sentences.en: So, this is the question, how is it that the British and the French have managed to win the Battle of the Alma when they are up against, you know, what is undoubtedly a really,
sentences.zh: 所以问题来了，英法联军怎么就能赢得阿尔马战役呢，当他们面对的无疑是一个真正、

sentences.en: really difficult position?
sentences.zh: 真正困难的阵地时？

sentences.en: I'll give you the answer that Cecil Woodham Smith, in The Reason Why, gave.
sentences.zh: 我把塞西尔·伍德姆·史密斯在《原因何在》中给出的答案告诉你。

sentences.en: It was a battle forever memorable for the ferocious courage of the British troops, so that's great, and the extraordinary incompetence displayed by the generals on both sides.
sentences.zh: 这是一场因英军的凶猛勇气而永远令人难忘的战役，这很好，还有双方将军所表现出的非凡无能。

sentences.en: What has been called the characteristic insanity of the Crimean War reached its height at the Alma.
sentences.zh: 克里米亚战争那种被称为特征性疯狂的东西在阿尔马达到了顶点。

sentences.en: Advantages were gained not through superior skill, but as a result of astonishing blunders made by each participant in turn.
sentences.zh: 优势的取得不是靠高超的技巧，而是由于各方轮流犯下的惊人错误。

sentences.en: So, basically, the Battle of the Alma is a succession of generals making catastrophic mistakes, and the Russians lose because their mistakes are worse.
sentences.zh: 所以，基本上，阿尔马战役就是一连串将军犯下灾难性的错误，而俄国人失败是因为他们的错误更严重。

sentences.en: But the British and the French, you know, they're chipping in in the whole field of military incompetence thing as well.
sentences.zh: 但英法联军呢，你知道，他们在整个军事无能的领域里也同样贡献了一份力。

sentences.en: You're telling me that Lord Raglan has not distinguished himself?
sentences.zh: 你是说拉格伦勋爵并没有表现出色？

sentences.en: No, he proves spectacularly inefficient, very, very ineffectual.
sentences.zh: 没有，他表现得极其低效，非常非常无能。

sentences.en: He doesn't really have a battle plan beyond kind of vaguely ordering his men to advance, which I think is, I mean, that's kind of beginner's level generalship.
sentences.zh: 他基本上没有什么作战计划，除了含糊不清地命令他的士兵前进，我认为这，我的意思是，这简直是初学者级别的将帅水平。

sentences.en: And the orders that he does give are, again, so ambiguously expressed as effectively to be incomprehensible.
sentences.zh: 而且他下达的命令，同样表达得如此含糊不清，以至于实际上无法理解。

sentences.en: And this is an issue with Raglan's orders that will be a theme throughout the rest of this series.
sentences.zh: 这是拉格伦命令的一个问题，这也将成为本系列余下部分的一个主题。

sentences.en: He also, I mean, this is mad, he rides forward and he kind of rides up to this knoll, which gives him a commanding position over the entire battlefield.
sentences.zh: 他还，我的意思是，这太疯狂了，他骑马向前冲到这个小山丘上，这让他对整个战场拥有居高临下的视野。

sentences.en: But it's so in advance of the rest of the army that he finds himself cut off by the Russian forces.
sentences.zh: 但它距离大部队太超前了，以至于他发现自己被俄军切断了退路。

sentences.en: Madly, I mean, a kind of despair of Russian incompetence, they don't come up and try and capture him.
sentences.zh: 疯狂的是，我的意思是，由于俄国人无能得令人绝望，他们没有上来试图俘虏他。

sentences.en: I was about to say, why don't they capture him?
sentences.zh: 我正想说，他们为什么不俘虏他？

sentences.en: Because they're useless.
sentences.zh: 因为他们太废柴了。

sentences.en: But Raglan is stuck on this knoll, and he can watch the battlefield, but he can't contribute to it.
sentences.zh: 但拉格伦被困在这个小山丘上，他能观察战场，却无法对战局做出贡献。

sentences.en: So that's basically him out of the deal.
sentences.zh: 所以基本上他已经出局了。

sentences.en: Santana, I mean, we've said he's got terminal stomach cancer, so you've got to cut him some slack.
sentences.zh: 圣阿尔诺，我的意思是，我们说过他得了晚期胃癌，所以你必须对他宽容一点。

sentences.en: But he, I mean, he's in such agony that the only way that he can kind of witness the battle is to take masses of opiates.
sentences.zh: 但他，我的意思是，他痛苦不堪，以至于目睹战斗的唯一方法就是服用大量的阿片类药物。

sentences.en: So he's basically propped up in his saddle off his face on drugs.
sentences.zh: 所以他基本上是靠在马鞍上，嗑药嗑得神志不清。

sentences.en: So it's kind of like, you know, Pete Doherty is running the battle for you, which again is kind of suboptimal.
sentences.zh: 所以这有点像，你知道的，皮特·多赫蒂在为你指挥战斗，这同样有点不太理想。

sentences.en: So neither Raglan nor Santana are really contributing much to the event.
sentences.zh: 所以拉格伦和圣阿尔诺都没有对战事做出什么实质贡献。

sentences.en: But as we've said, fortunately, Menchikov is even worse.
sentences.zh: 但正如我们所说，幸运的是，缅希科夫更糟糕。

sentences.en: And by far his most egregious blunder is to have assumed that the heights above the Alma were much more impregnable than they turn out to be.
sentences.zh: 他迄今为止最严重的失误，是认为阿尔马上方的高地比实际情况要坚不可摧得多。

sentences.en: And particularly on his left flank, so that's the flank that's nearest the sea, there are these towering cliffs.
sentences.zh: 特别是他的左翼，也就是离海最近的那侧侧翼，那里有高耸的悬崖。

sentences.en: And Menchikov had assumed that these were impassable, that no one would be able to get up the side.
sentences.zh: 缅希科夫原本以为这些是不可逾越的，没有人能够爬上去。

sentences.en: But the French, led by a guy called Pierre Bosquet, who amazingly is actually halfway competent, they storm their way up the cliffs.
sentences.zh: 但法国人在一个叫皮埃尔·博斯凯的家伙率领下，惊人地竟然有半斤八两的能力，他们一路冲上了悬崖。

sentences.en: They have some troops from Algeria who are very, a dab hand at climbing up a cliff.
sentences.zh: 他们有一些来自阿尔及利亚的部队，非常擅长爬悬崖。

sentences.en: And they get up there and then they kind of lower ropes and they all get up there.
sentences.zh: 他们上去了，然后放下绳子，大家就都上去了。

sentences.en: And these are the troops that set the ladies at their picnic flying back to Sebastopol.
sentences.zh: 正是这些军队把正在野餐的女士们吓得飞奔回塞瓦斯托波尔。

sentences.en: And they, the French get up there in kind of considerable force and they crash into the left flank of the Russian army.
sentences.zh: 法国人以相当规模的兵力登上了山崖，猛烈冲击俄军的左翼。

sentences.en: And this is the manoeuvre that effectively loses the Russians the battle.
sentences.zh: 这就是实际上让俄军输掉这场战役的战术机动。

sentences.en: But the British absolutely do their bit.
sentences.zh: 但英国人绝对尽到了他们的职责。

sentences.en: So if Raglan is useless, the pluck of the British Tommy is absolutely heroic.
sentences.zh: 所以如果拉格伦毫无用处，那么英国汤姆大兵的坚韧绝对是英雄般的。

sentences.en: And it's not English because actually the, well, I mean, the English absolutely do their bit.
sentences.zh: 而且不只是英格兰人，因为实际上，嗯，我的意思是，英格兰人绝对尽了力。

sentences.en: But the guys who absolutely are the heroes of the day are the Scots and more specifically, the three Highland regiments.
sentences.zh: 但绝对是当之无愧的英雄是苏格兰人，更具体地说，是三个高地团。

sentences.en: And they display amazing discipline and courage under fire.
sentences.zh: 他们在炮火下展现出了惊人的纪律和勇气。

sentences.en: So when the ladies are looking out and seeing the kind of the line of red advancing beneath withering shellfire up the slope, I mean, kind of amazing achievement.
sentences.zh: 所以当女士们向外望去，看到一排红色队伍在猛烈的炮火下沿着斜坡向上推进时，我的意思是，这真是一种惊人的成就。

sentences.en: The guys who are the most impressive are the Scots who, you know, have their kilts.
sentences.zh: 最让人印象深刻的是那些穿着苏格兰裙的苏格兰人。

sentences.en: So that's exciting for the ladies.
sentences.zh: 所以这让女士们感到很兴奋。

sentences.en: Yeah, they're wearing kilts.
sentences.zh: 对，他们穿着苏格兰裙。

sentences.en: And also, but they've sort of cheated by having a commander who knows what he's doing.
sentences.zh: 而且还有，他们某种程度上通过找一个知道自己在做什么的指挥官来作弊。

sentences.en: By having a meritocratic, non-aristocratic commander, haven't they?
sentences.zh: 通过找一个精英统治的、非贵族出身的指挥官，对吧？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So this is Sir Colin Campbell, who we mentioned before, veteran of wars in the Punjab and India more generally.
sentences.zh: 这就是我们前面提到的科林·坎贝尔爵士，旁遮普战争和更广泛的印度战争的老兵。

sentences.en: And he maneuvers his Highland regiments so effectively that they are able to attack an entire Russian column in its flank and take them out.
sentences.zh: 他非常有效地调动他的高地团，以至于他们能够袭击整个俄军纵队的侧翼并将其消灭。

sentences.en: But the great discovery that Campbell and his Highland regiments make is just how devastating a weapon they have in the form of the Minier, which was this rifle, you may remember.
sentences.zh: 但坎贝尔和他的高地团发现的伟大之处在于，他们拥有米尼式步枪这种极具毁灭性的武器，大家可能还记得。

sentences.en: Oh, yes.
sentences.zh: 哦，是的。

sentences.en: Had been introduced only the previous year by Viscount Harding, the commander in chief of the British Army.
sentences.zh: 这把枪是就在前一年由英国陆军总司令哈丁子爵引入的。

sentences.en: This weapon has never been used in anger before, but when it's unleashed on the battlefield of the Alma, it proves absolutely devastating.
sentences.zh: 这种武器以前从未在实战中使用过，但当它在阿尔玛战场上被释放时，它被证明具有绝对的毁灭性。

sentences.en: It has a much greater range, greater accuracy, greater penetration than the muskets that are being used by the Russians.
sentences.zh: 与俄军使用的滑膛枪相比，它具有更大的射程、更高的精度和更强的穿透力。

sentences.en: And to quote Orlando Fijis in his book on the Crimea, the volleys delivered an intensity of fire achieved by half a dozen machine guns.
sentences.zh: 用奥兰多·费吉斯在其克里米亚著作中的话说，齐射带来了半打机枪所达到的火力强度。

sentences.en: And this essentially is what enables the British, even though they are advancing uphill against forces that outnumber them to force the Russians back.
sentences.zh: 这基本上就是英国人能够迫使俄军后撤的原因，尽管他们是在向上坡冲锋，面对着在人数上占优势的军队。

sentences.en: And the fighting is very, very brutal.
sentences.zh: 而且战斗非常非常残酷。

sentences.en: And the British undoubtedly display the magnificent resolve and pluck for which the British soldier is renowned.
sentences.zh: 毫无疑问，英国士兵展现出了令英国士兵闻名遐迩的非凡决心和勇气。

sentences.en: But of course.
sentences.zh: 但当然。

sentences.en: But I think the Minier rifle is essentially what decides the battle, that and the French maneuver, you're getting up the cliffs.
sentences.zh: 但我觉得米尼式步枪基本上是决定战局的关键，还有就是法军的机动，你们爬上了悬崖。

sentences.en: So by late afternoon, the Russians are retreating, aren't they?
sentences.zh: 所以在傍晚时分，俄军正在撤退，对吧？

sentences.en: And the British and French have their first major kind of battlefield honors.
sentences.zh: 而英法联军赢得了他们第一个重大的战场荣誉。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: But obviously the question that will be on the minds of loads of listeners is, are heroes, Lord Cardigan and Lord Lucan, how are they getting on?
sentences.zh: 但很显然，广大听众心中最大的疑问会是，我们的英雄卡迪根勋爵和卢卡恩勋爵，他们最近怎么样？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: I mean, are they, are they buried the hatchet?
sentences.zh: 我是说，他们，他们言归于好了吗？

sentences.en: Are they leading the charge?
sentences.zh: 他们在带头发起冲锋吗？

sentences.en: Are they distinguishing themselves and writing their names into the annals of legend or not?
sentences.zh: 他们是在大显身手，把自己的名字写进传奇史册，还是没有？

sentences.en: No, no.
sentences.zh: 没有，没有。

sentences.en: So the battle of the armor has raged for three hours.
sentences.zh: 所以阿尔玛战役已经激战了三个小时。

sentences.en: And in all that time, the cavalry have done absolutely nothing.
sentences.zh: 而在所有这些时间里，骑兵什么也没做。

sentences.en: Oh.
sentences.zh: 哦。

sentences.en: I mean, Lucan and Cardigan, of course, have been rowing for three hours, but they haven't actually been turning their, their steel on the Russians.
sentences.zh: 我是说，卢卡恩和卡迪根当然已经争吵了三个小时，但他们实际上并没有把他们的刀刃转向俄军。

sentences.en: And the reason for that is the same as the day before, that Raglan, he just hasn't wanted to risk them.
sentences.zh: 原因和前一天一样，拉格朗根本不想冒险动用他们。

sentences.en: Um, I think if he'd had the heavy brigade, it's the job of the heavy brigade to attack infantry that, you know, that might've been different, but the light brigade,
sentences.zh: 嗯，我想如果他当时有重骑兵旅——重骑兵旅的任务就是攻击步兵——你知道，那可能会有所不同，但轻骑兵旅，

sentences.en: he's not prepared to risk them.
sentences.zh: 他不愿意让他们冒这个险。

sentences.en: You know, they're so outnumbered by the Russian cavalry.
sentences.zh: 你知道，他们在俄军骑兵面前人数太悬殊了。

sentences.en: And also the terrain is very unsuited to the operation of cavalry.
sentences.zh: 而且地形也非常不适合骑兵作战。

sentences.en: It's kind of, you know, it's hilly, it's broken, it's covered in scrub.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，那地方丘陵起伏，地形破碎，长满灌木。

sentences.en: It's not, not good at all.
sentences.zh: 一点都不好，完全不适合。

sentences.en: So actually, again, once again, Raglan is not doing this willfully or eccentrically.
sentences.zh: 所以实际上，拉格朗再次并不是出于固执或古怪才这么做的。

sentences.en: I mean, he's making good decisions.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他做出了正确的决定。

sentences.en: No, he's not.
sentences.zh: 不，他没有。

sentences.en: Um, I mean, he's keeping them in a band box, but two things to say about Raglan and the cavalry.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我的意思是，他把他们保护得好好的，但关于拉格朗和骑兵有两点要说。

sentences.en: I mean, Raglan can't actually get his orders to them because he's stuck on this knoll.
sentences.zh: 我是说，拉格朗实际上无法把命令传达给他们，因为他被困在这个小山丘上了。

sentences.en: Oh yeah, of course.
sentences.zh: 哦对，当然。

sentences.en: So even if an opportunity had come where he might've wanted to use them, he wouldn't be able to give it.
sentences.zh: 所以即使出现了他可能想用他们的机会，他也无法下达命令。

sentences.en: But the other thing is that as the Russians start breaking formation and withdrawing and then turning their backs and going into a full blown retreat, I mean,
sentences.zh: 但另一件事是，当俄军开始打破队形撤退，然后转过身去全面溃退时，我是说，

sentences.en: this is classically the moment when if you are a general, you do unleash your light cavalry on the enemy.
sentences.zh: 经典上这就是当你是将领时，你该对敌人释放轻骑兵的时刻。

sentences.en: Um, because this is the opportunity to really finish off a foe when they're, that when they're broken, when they're in retreat, Lukan and Raglan have been arguing for three hours,
sentences.zh: 嗯，因为这是一个真正彻底消灭敌人的机会，当他们被打垮、当他们在撤退时。卢卡恩和拉格朗已经争吵了三个小时，

sentences.en: but watching the Russians in full blown retreat, this is something they can agree on.
sentences.zh: 但看着全面溃退的俄军，这是他们意见一致的事情。

sentences.en: They really should be having a crack at them.
sentences.zh: 他们确实应该给敌人致命一击。

sentences.en: So, uh, one of the officers in their train describes the Russians, they're running as hard as they could, throwing away their knapsacks, arms,
sentences.zh: 所以，嗯，他们随行的一名军官这样描述俄军：他们拼命逃跑，扔掉了背包、武器，

sentences.en: even their coats to assist them in their flight.
sentences.zh: 甚至连大衣都扔了，只为了逃跑时轻便一点。

sentences.en: Like surely they're thinking, you know, let us, let us, let us do what we're here to do.
sentences.zh: 就像他们肯定在想，你知道的，让我们去，让我们去，让我们去做我们来这儿该做的事。

sentences.en: Yeah, absolutely.
sentences.zh: 对，绝对的。

sentences.en: But Raglan says, no, by this point he's rejoined the mass of his army and two times Lukan basically ignores his orders.
sentences.zh: 但拉格朗说，不，此时他已经重新加入了他的大部队，而且卢卡恩基本上两次无视他的命令。

sentences.en: You know, he, Raglan saying, do not attack.
sentences.zh: 你知道，拉格朗说，不要进攻。

sentences.en: Lukan ignores it.
sentences.zh: 卢卡恩不理睬。

sentences.en: He's riding the cavalry are up to have a go at the Russians.
sentences.zh: 他正骑着马带着骑兵去袭击俄军。

sentences.en: And the third time, um, Raglan tears him off a strip and says, you know, you are being insubordinate.
sentences.zh: 第三次，嗯，拉格朗严厉训斥了他一顿并说道，你知道的，你这是在抗命。

sentences.en: Do as you are ordered.
sentences.zh: 按你的命令办事。

sentences.en: I am not going to let the light brigade go after the fleeing Russians.
sentences.zh: 我绝不会让轻骑兵去追击逃跑的俄军。

sentences.en: So this is terrible for Lukan.
sentences.zh: 这对卢卡恩来说太糟糕了。

sentences.en: But what rubs salt massively in the wounds is that most of the cavalry, again, do not blame Raglan for this, but blame Lukan himself, Lord Lukan.
sentences.zh: 但更让人伤口上撒盐的是，大多数骑兵再次没有责怪拉格朗，而是责怪卢卡恩本人，卢卡恩勋爵。

sentences.en: And again, it's so unfair.
sentences.zh: 而且这太不公平了。

sentences.en: I mean, Lukan is, you know, it's not true at all, but this is what the cavalry think.
sentences.zh: 我是说，卢卡恩，你知道的，这完全不是真的，但这正是骑兵们的想法。

sentences.en: And that evening, one cavalry officer in particular, he comes storming into the tent of William Russell, the Times correspondent.
sentences.zh: 那天晚上，特别是有一名骑兵军官，气势汹汹地冲进了《泰晤士报》特派员威廉·拉塞尔的帐篷。

sentences.en: And he goes public with what he's thinking with his kind of sense of absolute indignation and rage.
sentences.zh: 他公开表达了自己的想法，带着那种绝对的愤慨和愤怒。

sentences.en: And he tells Russell, there were 1000 British cavalry looking on at a beaten army retreating.
sentences.zh: 他告诉拉塞尔，有一千名英国骑兵在冷眼旁观一支被打败的军队撤退。

sentences.en: It is enough to drive one mad.
sentences.zh: 这简直能把人逼疯。

sentences.en: It is too disgraceful, too infamous.
sentences.zh: 这太可耻了，太卑劣了。

sentences.en: And what makes this outburst all the more startling is that it's coming from a member of Lord Raglan's own staff.
sentences.zh: 而让这种情绪爆发更令人震惊的是，它来自于拉格朗勋爵自己幕僚的一名成员。

sentences.en: And this is a captain.
sentences.zh: 这是一位上尉。

sentences.en: His name is Lewis Edward Nolan.
sentences.zh: 他的名字叫刘易斯·爱德华·诺兰。

sentences.en: And he's universally regarded as the most brilliant young officer in the entire cavalry.
sentences.zh: 他被普遍认为是整个骑兵部队中最才华横溢的年轻军官。

sentences.en: So much so that Cardigan had wanted him for his own staff and Raglan had poached him.
sentences.zh: 正因如此，卡迪根曾想把他招入自己的幕僚，但被拉格朗抢先挖走了。

sentences.en: And he's a very interesting man, isn't he, with a sort of remarkable background.
sentences.zh: 他是一个非常有趣的人，对吧，有着一段非凡的背景。

sentences.en: I mean, he is massively woke by the standards of the British army.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，按英国陆军的标准来看，他思想极度前卫（觉醒）。

sentences.en: Well, we'll come to his wokeness.
sentences.zh: 好吧，我们等会儿会谈到他的前卫。

sentences.en: I mean, he's very brave.
sentences.zh: 我是说，他非常勇敢。

sentences.en: He's very intelligent and he's very dashing.
sentences.zh: 他非常聪明，而且非常意气风发。

sentences.en: And his upbringing, as you say, has been unusual, I think.
sentences.zh: 正如你所说，他的成长经历很不寻常，我认为。

sentences.en: So his father was an Irish major and had served in Milan as the British vice consul there.
sentences.zh: 他的父亲是一名爱尔兰少校，曾在米兰担任英国副领事。

sentences.en: And so Nolan had grown up in Italy speaking Italian.
sentences.zh: 所以诺兰是在意大利长大的，会说意大利语。

sentences.en: And he'd, throughout his teens, shown an amazing aptitude for horsemanship.
sentences.zh: 在整个青少年时期，他表现出了惊人的骑马天赋。

sentences.en: And at the age of 17, he's talent spotted by an Austrian recruiting officer and given a commission in what's inevitably described as a crack Austrian cavalry regiment.
sentences.zh: 在17岁时，他被一名奥地利征兵官慧眼识珠，在一支不可避免地被描述为顶尖的奥地利骑兵团中获得了军官职位。

sentences.en: Always, surely.
sentences.zh: 那当然了。

sentences.en: I bet they've got tremendous uniforMs.
sentences.zh: 我敢打赌他们的制服一定帅呆了。

sentences.en: Oh, magnificent.
sentences.zh: 哦，华丽极了。

sentences.en: And he sees service because he serves in Hungary and on the frontier with Russian-held Poland.
sentences.zh: 他服过兵役，因为他在匈牙利以及俄占波兰边境服役过。

sentences.en: And he learns Hungarian, Dominic, like you.
sentences.zh: 他学会了匈牙利语，多米尼克，就像你一样。

sentences.en: So he's, you know, a master of Balkan languages.
sentences.zh: 所以他，你知道的，精通巴尔干语言。

sentences.en: Brilliant.
sentences.zh: 太棒了。

sentences.en: He'd been pals with Imre Nodg in another life.
sentences.zh: 他在另一段人生中曾与伊姆雷·纳吉是好朋友。

sentences.en: Yeah, I'm not sure if he would.
sentences.zh: 对，我不确定他是否会这样。

sentences.en: I think he'd have found Imre Nodg slightly drab.
sentences.zh: 我觉得他会觉得伊姆雷·纳吉有点乏味。

sentences.en: The Nodgster?
sentences.zh: 纳吉斯特？

sentences.en: What?
sentences.zh: 什么？

sentences.en: Mad.
sentences.zh: 疯了。

sentences.en: No, the Nodgster's not into cavalry.
sentences.zh: 不，纳吉斯特对骑兵不感兴趣。

sentences.en: I think it's safely say that's one thing he absolutely wasn't into.
sentences.zh: 我想可以确切地说，那是他绝对不感兴趣的一件事。

sentences.en: Anyway, but this is moot because he doesn't stay in Hungary.
sentences.zh: 无论如何，但这并不重要，因为他没有留在匈牙利。

sentences.en: He doesn't stay in Austria because he is reproached by a visiting British officer for a lack of patriotism.
sentences.zh: 他没有留在奥地利，因为他被一名来访的英国军官指责缺乏爱国主义。

sentences.en: He says you should be devoting your tremendous talents for horsemanship in the service of your queen and country.
sentences.zh: 他说，你应该把你非凡的骑马天赋奉献给你的女王和国家。

sentences.en: And so Nolan feels the sting of this reproach and he joins the 15th Hussars and very quickly establishes a reputation for himself that is international in scale.
